title: StratusLink & Redwood: Open Ops Partner Discovery
next_steps: Redwood to send partner integration deck and pricing template
StratusLink to share architecture diagram and expected QPS profile
Schedule technical POC baseline tests w/ dedicated SE + StratusLink ops (target week of 8/26)
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 report
action_items: Maya Chen; Send partner integration deck + draft SOW; 2025-08-15
Devon Shah; Provide expected GPU types + steady-state QPS and p99 latency targets; 2025-08-20
Tom Nguyen; Share completed security questionnaire and list of required controls; 2025-08-18

summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and StratusLink to evaluate a channel + technical integration: StratusLink wants a turnkey onramp for customers to run LLM inference via their managed infra. Discussion covered private vs hosted flows, dedicated GPU pools, network isolation (VPC peering vs transit), KMS/HSM key management, and a preliminary POC scope to validate throughput and latency targets.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-13
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Imani Patel (Redwood Product), Alicia Park (StratusLink Head Partnerships), Devon Shah (StratusLink GPU Ops Lead), Tom Nguyen (StratusLink Security Architect), Priya Nair (StratusLink SE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining — i'm Maya with Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this motion, joining me is Carlos SE, Imani from product. happy to kick off, also we have the partner deck linked in the chat — https://redwood.ai/partner-deck (shared).
[00:18] Alicia Park: thanks Maya, excited to do this quick sync. we spun up a small partnership team to look at onramps for customers that need low-latency inference on their models. StratusLink runs managed GPU pools across colo + cloud, and we've gotten a few requests to integrate third-party serving runtimes.
[00:34] Carlos Rivera: great, can you give a bit more context about the types of customers? e.g., enterprise with strict data residency, or ai-native startups?
[00:44] Alicia Park: mix — about 60% enterprises (regulated), 40% startups. typical ask: private deployment or managed VPC peering, encryption at rest and in transit, and sometimes an on-prem air-gapped option.
[00:56] Devon Shah: and from ops side we care about GPU efficiency — customers want to avoid huge overspend. they ask about batching, quantization, and multi-tenant isolation.
[01:08] Imani Patel: yeah that's exactly where Redwood Optimize and our runtime help — intelligent batching, KV prefix caching, quantization profiles. happy to walk through tradeoffs.
[01:18] Priya Nair: quick Q — how do you handle KMS keys in private deployments? some customers require HSM-backed keys and customer-managed KMS.
[01:28] Maya Chen: in Redwood Private we support bring-your-own-KMS, HSM via partner integrations, and audit logs for key usage. note we also offer dedicated capacity where Redwood manages key wrapping but with strict tenancy.
[01:40] Tom Nguyen: transcription: so you have both a private control plane and an option to run the data plane entirely in customer VPC? what's the latency hit for routing control plane calls?
[01:52] Carlos Rivera: yes we have a split-plane model. control plane can be hosted or run in customer's VPC; data plane stays in-customer for private install. latency depends more on network path and batch sizing — for typical gen workloads we aim for low 100s ms p50 on Llama2 13B class with dedicated NVLink pools. (note: transcript sometimes says 'Llama to' or 'laminar').
[02:18] Alicia Park: can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private? folks here used 'dedicated' and 'private' interchangeably earlier.
[02:26] Maya Chen: brief: Hosted Redwood API = our cloud. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools we operate for a single customer on our infra (isolated tenancy). Private = customer-managed deployment (VPC or on-prem) where control plane may still be Redwood-managed optionally. dedicated is faster to onboard; private gives max data control.
[02:44] Devon Shah: if we wanted to offer Redwood's runtime as an option on StratusLink — do you support multi-tenant lane isolation? e.g., multiple customers using same GPU pool but with strong isolation?
[02:56] Carlos Rivera: we have tenancy controls and container-level isolation. for multi-tenant we recommend soft partitioning with strict quotas and per-tenant KV namespace. for high-security customers we suggest dedicated pools.
[03:10] Priya Nair: about audits: customers ask for SOC2 + iso 27001. do you have reports we can share with our customers?
[03:18] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO report are available under NDA — we'll share them. also we provide per-request audit logs and token-level billing to help you with chargebacks.
[03:28] Tom Nguyen: great, please send. also we need details on encryption in flight — do you use mTLS for inter-service comms?
[03:36] Carlos Rivera: mTLS for internal services and TLS for external. for private installs you can configure your certs and we support customer-supplied CA.
[03:44] Alicia Park: on the commercial side, how do you price dedicated pools vs hosted? our channel model usually takes a margin.
[03:52] Maya Chen: hosted is usage-based (per token / per-embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. for partnerships we can provide a reseller pricing template; that's part of the partner packet.
[04:06] Imani Patel: one thing we often highlight: cost controls — batching and KV caching often reduce per-token costs dramatically for repetitive prompts. this is sometimes a surprise to customers who expect linear costs.
[04:18] Devon Shah: on benchmarks — we need to validate sustained throughput for models customers deploy. what harness do you recommend for end-to-end POC?
[04:26] Carlos Rivera: we can share a benchmark harness (python based) that simulates streaming loads and measures p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and token cost. we'll also run a small smoke with your infra to identify network bottlenecks.
[04:40] Alicia Park: good. next: network topology. StratusLink prefers VPC peering to avoid public egress. does Redwood support peering and cross-account roles for provisioning?
[04:52] Maya Chen: yes we support VPC peering, PrivateLink-like setups, and cross-account IAM roles for resource provisioning. for on-prem we rely on site-to-site VPN or direct connect equivalents.
[05:02] Tom Nguyen: what about data residency? some customers want logs never leave the customer's region. can you pin model inference to region and keep telemetry local?
[05:12] Carlos Rivera: yes, routing policies allow pinning by region/customer tier. telemetry retention is configurable in private deployments; hosted customers can request retention SLAs.
[05:24] Priya Nair: curious about model variants — if we route to smaller quantized variants for cost reasons, does Redwood offer automatic quality regression alerts?
[05:33] Imani Patel: we do: Redwood Optimize provides evals and quality monitoring; you can attach prompt sets and the system raises regression alerts when metrics drop. it helps guard against regressions when switching quantized models.
[05:46] Alicia Park: let's talk POC scope. idea: StratusLink will provision a small NVLink cluster with 4x A100-equivalent nodes, and Redwood will deploy runtime in a customer VPC and run two models under load for 24 hrs to validate throughput and p99. is that realistic?
[06:02] Carlos Rivera: yes, that's doable. we'd want sample prompt distributions, expected concurrency, and a success criteria matrix (p50 < 200ms ; p99 < 1.2s ; token cost <$0.0008 for given model) — those numbers are examples, we can adjust.
[06:18] Devon Shah: the cost per token target is heavily model-dependent. do you recommend quantization to 4-bit for the throughput gains?
[06:26] Imani Patel: for many workloads 4-bit quant is a good tradeoff; we ship quantization profiles per model. some customers prefer 8-bit for quality-sensitive cases.
[06:34] Priya Nair: for the POC we need to understand security gating: network rules, KMS integration, where logs are stored. we'll put together a minimal security checklist.
[06:44] Tom Nguyen: when you say 'KV cache' are you caching prefixes only or full KV for streaming? transcription heard 'K-V cash' earlier which made me laugh.
[06:52] Carlos Rivera: (laughs) prefix/KV caching — we persist key-value caches for attention states to speed up autoregressive decoding, reducing repeated compute for similar prefixes. it's configurable per-route.
[07:06] [07:06] Alicia Park: are there any red flags we should be aware of if we surface this to our legal/compliance teams?
[07:12] Maya Chen: main asks will be data residency, auditability, encryption, and SLAs. we provide an enterprise package with SOC2, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, VPC options, and dedicated retention windows.
[07:26] Devon Shah: one more ops Q: how do you handle autoscaling — burst vs reserved? we need to understand cold start behaviors for model loading.
[07:36] Carlos Rivera: autoscaling policies can be configured with warm pools and pre-warmed instances. cold start for large models is non-trivial; we recommend either warming or keeping a small warm standby for p99-sensitive routes. startup time depends on model size and quantization; we can often get <30s warm with warmed caches and async load strategies.
[07:58] Imani Patel: also worth noting: our kernel selection and compilation can change startup profile; for some hardware we precompile kernels to reduce first-run latency.
[08:10] Maya Chen: okay last section — commercial and partnership mechanics. Alicia, how do you envision StratusLink packaging this for customers? reseller? co-managed?
[08:20] Alicia Park: probably as an add-on: StratusLink manages infra + onboarding, Redwood runtime optional as 'managed inference engine' that customers can subscribe to through StratusLink. we want a clear reseller margin and simple support handoff.
[08:34] Maya Chen: we have a reseller program and partner SLAs; we can draft a partner pricing addendum. I'll include a pricing template in the packet.
[08:44] Devon Shah: any references from other partners who've done similar integrations?
[08:50] Maya Chen: yes we recently did a channel onramp with ArborLink and EdgeGrid — I'll share the anonymized case study. (note: transcript may say 'Arbor bank' in places).
[09:00] Priya Nair: timeline — we need this to be quick. if we agree on POC, can we turn around infra and smoke tests within two weeks?
[09:08] Carlos Rivera: yes with mutual readiness we can run smoke tests within 7-10 business days and a 2-week POC after that.
[09:16] Alicia Park: perfect. can we capture recap and next steps on the call?
[09:22] Maya Chen: yes — recap: Redwood to send partner deck, pricing template, SOC2 and reference case study; StratusLink to send architecture diagram, GPU inventory, and security checklist. propose technical kickoff week of 8/26. action items will be in the follow-up.
[09:38] Tom Nguyen: small nit: for the security questionnaire we'll need to add questions about key escrow, tenant separation, and log retention windows.
[09:46] Carlos Rivera: noted. we'll have our security PM plug that into the questionnaire.
[09:52] Priya Nair: one last ops thing — if we route requests from StratusLink customers to Redwood-managed dedicated pools, how do you handle DDoS protection and capacity spikes?
[10:02] Maya Chen: we have rate-limiting, throttles, and burst capacity. for channel partners we can pre-provision burst pools or set up fallback routing to lower-cost variants. DDoS protection is layered with cloud provider and our WAF.
[10:18] Alicia Park: ok thanks. any final Qs?
[10:22] Devon Shah: none here. excited to see the deck.
[10:26] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invite for POC kickoff.

[crosstalk and smaller chat as people start to drop off, transcription becomes slightly garbled in places: 'red book' for Redwood, 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'laminar' for Llama2]

[End of meeting — approx 58 mins]

Notes on transcript quality: audio had one speaker on VPN with echo; some proper nouns mis-transcribed (see above). Reference links shared: partner deck (https://redwood.ai/partner-deck), benchmark harness repo (internal link to be shared), SOC2 report (NDA required).
